Haploinsufficiency of SOX2 disrupts the regulation of embryonic stem cell differentiation pathways, leading to the developmental defects observed in both anophthalmia/microphthalmia-esophageal atresia syndrome and FOXP1 syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SOX2 that are exclusively associated with one disease phenotype but not the other, or evidence of a distinct molecular pathway disrupted in each disease. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a pathogenic variant in SOX2 with a population frequency >0.001)_

Haploinsufficiency of FOXP1 disrupts neuronal development, which in turn can also disrupt left-right asymmetry, leading to heterotaxy, and also directly leads to intellectual disability.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of ZIC3 variants in individuals with intellectual disability and absence of FOXP1 variants in individuals with heterotaxy would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if ZIC3 variants are found to be exclusively associated with heterotaxy and FOXP1 variants exclusively with intellectual disability without any overlap in phenotypic presentation or underlying pathway disruption, this would also weaken the proposed link.
